labels.placement: At each service equipment location to which the PV system(s) are connected, or an approved readily visible location (main service disconnect / meter-main).
On the rapid-shutdown initiation device and/or at the array boundary where conductor-control type must be identified.
On or within 1 m (3 ft) of the rapid-shutdown switch / initiation device.
On the DC / PV system disconnecting means enclosure.
On PV system disconnecting means where line and load terminals may be energized in the open position (typical of PV disconnects fed from both directions).
On DC disconnects, combiner boxes, and inverter DC input where energized terminals are accessible.
On exposed raceways, cable trays, cable assemblies, enclosures, combiner/junction box covers, and at intervals not exceeding 10 ft (3 m) and at turns/above-below penetrations.
On the DC PV system disconnecting means or the PV electronic power conversion equipment (inverter/optimizer).
On the AC disconnecting means at the point of interconnection.
On the exterior AC disconnect switch (typically near the utility meter).
On the distribution equipment (main panel/subpanel) adjacent to the back-fed breaker from the PV/power source.
On the main service panel / meter-main and any panel fed by more than one source.
At each service equipment location or an approved readily visible location.
At the supply-side connection point and on the service equipment/meter-main.
On the utility meter / service disconnect.
At each external access point to the ESS and at the main service disconnect.
At grounding electrode conductor terminations, array equipment-ground bonding points, and irreversible ground connections.
On the inverter / power conversion equipment enclosure.

after.remaining705_12Mentions: Every remaining 705.12 mention in the package is an explicitly NEGATED contrast ("the 120% busbar rule (NEC 705.12(B)) does not apply to supply-side connections" / "N/A" / "applies only load-side"). None is rendered as this design's governing interconnection article.
